claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows directly from the lesson's own definition (claim 1) applied to outline item 3; no factual dependency beyond claim 6, which was verified by execution (the subtype throws where the base declaration accepts any int).

"Base class members marked with the abstract keyword require that derived classes override them. Attempting to compile the following example generates compiler error CS0534, '<class> does not implement inherited abstract member <member>'" (inheritance.md:76). The 'enforced by the compiler' half is a behaviour fact, not opinion; see issue on ledger kind.

issues.text: Overstated: compiling a subclass checks far more than signatures (the method bodies are type-checked too). What the lesson needs is that compiling says nothing about which inputs the override accepts or throws for.
issues.quote: Actually compiling only proves the method signatures match.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Actually compiling proves the override has the right signature and its body is valid C#, not what it does for each input."

issues.text: Claims ledger: claim 8 is filed as kind `opinion`, but its first half ("Implementing every abstract method is enforced by the compiler") is compiler behaviour (CS0534) that needs a source, not an opinion.
issues.quote: Implementing every abstract method is enforced by the compiler and is not what LSP adds; LSP concerns behaviour.
issues.fix: In design.l1.solid-lsp.meta.json set claim 8 `kind` to `behavior`, `needs_verification` to true, `source_hint` to "C# docs: inheritance tutorial (abstract members), CS0534". No lesson text change.
